name: delirium overview
title: Delirium decision chart: a 4-AT of 4 or more means possible delirium, then hunt every trigger (DIMES + 3 Ps): drugs and the environment, acute illness, and pee, poo and pain that the patient may not report; each column gives what to look for, how to find it and how to treat it

root.title: Acutely confused older adult: DELIRIUM? Then FIND THE TRIGGER
lines: delirium = an ACUTE, FLUCTUATING change in attention and awareness
the QUIET one is missed: HYPOACTIVE (drowsy, lethargic) is the commonest, mistaken for DEPRESSION
screen with the 4-AT: < 2 minutes, no special training

groups.title: 4-AT ≥ 4: POSSIBLE DELIRIUM → hunt EVERY trigger (DIMES + 3 Ps)
lines: • clearly abnormal ALERTNESS, or an ACUTE change / fluctuation: 4 points EACH
• 1–3: possible cognitive impairment (COGNITIVE DECLINE chart) · 0: neither

columns.drop_label: D + E: what we gave or changed
head: h
Drugs · Environment
look: • glasses, hearing aids out of reach
tx: • sleep: less noise and light, ear plugs
• mobilize early, fewest restraints, family at the bedside
Drugs for SYMPTOMS: NOT evidence based
• hyperactive: antipsychotic first; watch the QT; avoid in seizures, Parkinson's, Lewy body dementia

head: h
Infection · Metabolic · Structural
look: It may show ONLY as delirium
atypical presentations: see the FRAILTY AND FALLS chart
tx: Slow to clear? Hunt for NEW triggers

head: h
Pee · Poo · Pain
find: Examine even if they deny it
